$comment: Provenance: read from courier at a8f15ccef11bd6148c71fbe38327d9fbebbfe2e2, and THE PUBLISHER IS NOT THERE. lib/courier/events.ex at that commit has `delivered/1`, `bounced/1`, `complained/1` and `suppressed/1`, and no `queued/1` — fleet.yml records the same fact in prose. So this schema is transcribed from courier's four sibling builders and from what `Courier.Deliver`'s payload actually contains, and it is NOT read from code that emits it. It is the one schema here that describes a publisher which does not exist yet, and it says so rather than letting the citation imply otherwise: when courier builds `queued/1`, this comment and the obligation it carries are what have to be revisited. The commit is fleet.yml's sourceCommit for courier.
title: courier.email.queued payload
description: The `data` payload of the `courier.email.queued` event: a message was accepted for delivery. Emitted on acceptance, not on send, so a queue backlog is visible before it becomes a support ticket. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

message_id.description: The notification. Always equal to the envelope's `subject`, and equal to the `message_id` on the `courier.email.delivered`, `.bounced` and `.complained` events about the same send — which is what lets a consumer measure how long a message waited.

user_id.description: The user the message is for. A bare uuid, not a cafaye-prefixed id: that is what identity emits. The two used not to join, because this repository said otherwise about identity's own events — see D7, whose second half was false, and D35 for the correction.

notification_type.description: Which of courier's three messages this is. The same three the preferences table is keyed by, so a consumer can ask whether the user had asked for this one.

email.description: The address the message goes to, as the caller supplied it. Present because a consumer that has to ask "who is this for?" in order to act on it will not — and because a suppression decision is about an address.
